items.stem: What does a support vector machine try to maximise?

options.text: The margin between classes around the decision boundary
options.rationale: Correct: SVMs maximise the separating margin.
It does not maximise the count of support vectors.

options.text: The depth of a decision tree

options.rationale: Learning rate is not the SVM objective.

items.explanation: Correct: SVMs maximise the separating margin.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about SVM practice are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Feature scaling is usually important for good SVM performance
options.rationale: Correct: SVMs are sensitive to feature scale.

options.text: The kernel trick allows non-linear boundaries without explicit high-dimensional features
SVMs always scale effortlessly to millions of rows
options.rationale: Standard SVMs can scale poorly on very large data.

options.text: Kernels create brand-new real data points
options.rationale: Kernels transform similarity, not add data.

items.explanation: Correct: SVMs are sensitive to feature scale.

items.stem: Increasing the C parameter in a soft-margin SVM tends to:

options.text: Penalise misclassifications more, allowing a narrower margin
options.rationale: Correct: larger C prioritises correct classification over a wide margin.

options.text: Always widen the margin regardless of errors
options.rationale: Larger C typically narrows the margin.

options.text: Turn the SVM into a decision tree
options.rationale: C does not change the model family.

items.explanation: Correct: larger C prioritises correct classification over a wide margin.
